St Paul by the numbers

Which county sends the St. Paul property tax bill?

Ramsey County does. Its Assessor values every St. Paul parcel, and its Property Tax Services unit mails the statements and takes the money. The capital city was incorporated on March 4, 1854, covers 51.97 square miles of land plus 4.13 of water on the Mississippi, and held 306,684 people in July 2025 according to Census QuickFacts, a 1.5% dip from the April 2020 base.

County property offices share the Plato Building at 90 Plato Blvd. West, Saint Paul, MN 55107, with front-desk service on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. Direct lines worth saving:

  • Property Tax Services, 651-266-2222: statements, payments, penalties
  • County Assessor, 651-266-2131: value and classification
  • Homestead Unit, 651-266-2040: applications and ITIN filing
  • Delinquent taxes, 651-266-2002: balances, interest, plans
  • Recorder's Office, 651-266-2050: deeds and other recorded real estate documents

How does St. Paul housing compare with the rest of Minnesota?

Owners and renters split the city almost evenly. QuickFacts shows owners in 52.9% of occupied homes across 2020 to 2024, spread over 125,249 households averaging 2.37 people.

  • A typical owned home was valued at $294,500, and owners with a mortgage spent $1,911 monthly.
  • Rent in the middle of the market ran $1,281 a month.
  • Households earned $73,394 in the middle, and 43.8% of adults held a bachelor's degree or more.
  • Workers traveled 21.1 minutes each way, and 83.7% of residents had lived at the same address the year before.
  • Land density in 2020 was 5,994 people per square mile.

Your bill hinges on classification. Ramsey County posts separate calculators for homestead against non-homestead houses, duplexes and triplexes, commercial buildings and apartments of four or more units, so check which category your parcel falls into before estimating a tax figure.

On which dates must St. Paul owners pay property tax?

Two installments, May 15 and October 15, cover real property, and a due date that falls on a weekend slides to Monday. Anyone with an escrow account at a mortgage company can skip the paperwork, since the lender pays. A bill of $100 or less must be settled whole with the first installment.

When each kind of Ramsey County bill is due (county Pay Property Tax page)
TypeFirst installmentSecond installment
Real propertyMay 15October 15
AgriculturalMay 15October 15
Leased government-owned personal propertyMay 15October 15
Other personal propertyMay 15, total dueNone
Manufactured homesAugust 31November 15

Each property gets two mailings a year. Mid-March brings the tax statement together with the value notice that drives next year's tax. In November the proposed tax notice follows, listing next year's proposed amounts and the meetings where levies and budgets are discussed. Owners may switch to electronic delivery through eNoticesOnline.

What does a late St. Paul payment cost?

Penalty starts the day after a due date, grows month by month, and is applied to penalty before tax when you pay. For a homestead or cabin, the 2026 first half picks up 2% on May 16, 4% on June 1, 5% on July 1 and 8% by October 1, then 10% on January 2, 2027. Non-homestead property climbs through 4%, 8%, 9% and 12% to 14% on those same dates.

A missed second half begins on October 16 at 2% for a homestead and 4% for a non-homestead, ending January 2 at 7% and 11%. Owing both halves on October 16 means 5% for a homestead and 8% otherwise.

The county offers two ways to soften a penalty:

  • One-time waiver: once per parcel in any 10-year span, for the first half or the second but not both. A first-half request must arrive from May 16 through October 15, and a second-half request from October 16 through December 20, with payment and the signed form. A waiver is refused if the payment bounced, if delinquent tax or a confession of judgment sits on the parcel, or if the waiver was already used in the past decade.
  • Hardship abatement: ask the County Auditor/Treasurer at 651-266-2222. The county grants these mainly for exceptional hardship such as a hospital stay.

Returned checks cost $30, and partial payments are accepted.

What can I do if I think my St. Paul value is wrong?

Phone the Assessor at 651-266-2131 before anything else. The county warns that you will not reach an appraiser on the spot: you describe the concern, and an appraiser calls back within three days. Mail or email a recent appraisal or a sale of your own property to back a claim of overvaluation or a wrong class.

State law requires a physical review of each parcel at least once every five years, and Ramsey County appraisers walk nearly 32,000 properties a year without advance notice. An interactive map on the county site shows when your area is due.

Homestead status lowers the bill, and the Homestead page lists what a seller or buyer should know:

  • The state exclusion trims taxable value only on homes valued below $517,200.
  • Homestead also counts toward the state Property Tax Refund.
  • A buyer must own and occupy the home by December 31 and apply by that date to qualify for the current assessment year.
  • An ITIN may replace a Social Security number on the filing.

How does Ramsey County treat delinquent St. Paul tax?

A bill becomes delinquent on January 1 of the next year. From then, interest accrues at 10% a year, rising monthly, and a $25 fee covers publication and notice. Owners then have three years to pay in full and redeem, or they can enter a payment plan called a Confession of Judgment.

If redemption lapses without payment, forfeiture begins, and the county notifies the owner in stages:

  • A courtesy letter in the first week of April
  • A parcel list in the county's newspaper for two weeks in May
  • The same list posted at the Property Records and Property Tax Services offices
  • Delivery of the notice by the sheriff to an occupant, or a posting at vacant and land-only property
  • A certified letter in June

Payments are applied to penalties first, then interest, fees and finally tax. A parcel may be paid after the list is printed, so call the delinquent line before assuming it is still on it.

What should a St. Paul seller ask for before closing?

Ask Property Tax Services for the parcel's exact balance, because the first half may be settled while the second is open, or both may be owed. Also ask where the account sits on the penalty schedule, since the rate steps up on June 1, July 1, October 16 and other dates.

Deeds and similar papers are recorded through the Recorder's Office, which keeps the county's official real estate records. It does not help fill out legal forms. A recorded document is permanent and cannot be removed or altered, so have a title company or attorney review the deed before it is filed.

More questions about St. Paul, MN Property Tax Guide

Which agency collects St. Paul's property tax?

Ramsey County Property Tax Services, in the Plato Building at 90 Plato Blvd. West. Reach it at 651-266-2222 on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.

When do St. Paul real property installments fall due?

May 15 and October 15. A weekend date moves to the next business day, and manufactured homes use August 31 and November 15 instead.

Is there a way to avoid a late St. Paul property tax penalty?

A one-time waiver exists, usable once per parcel every 10 years for one installment. Submit the signed form with your payment before the county's deadline for that half.

Who reviews a disputed St. Paul property value?

The County Assessor, at 651-266-2131. An appraiser returns your call within three days, and a recent appraisal or sale of the home can be sent as support.

What redemption window applies to delinquent tax on a St. Paul home?

Three years to pay everything owed, with payment plans available. The delinquent line, 651-266-2002, can give the current balance and interest.

Rochester by the numbers

Who bills property tax on a Rochester, Minnesota house?

Rochester homeowners get their tax bill from Olmsted County, whose assessor's office decides what each house is worth for tax purposes. That single bill folds in what the county, city hall, the schools and any special districts levy on your parcel.

The office that takes your payment is Olmsted County Property Records and Licensing, at the Government Center, 151 4th Street SE, Rochester, MN 55904. Dial 507-328-7636 about statements, 507-328-7635 about delinquent years, and 507-328-7670 for the assessor.

About 76,000 parcels countywide are valued as of each January 2, and state law ties the estimate to market value. Your value notice reaches you in mid-March alongside the tax statement. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate puts Rochester at 124,292 residents, third in Minnesota. See the county's property assessments page for the valuation side.

When are Rochester property taxes due, and what does a late payment cost?

Rochester owners pay in two installments, one in mid-May and one in mid-October. The county's 2026 schedule sets separate dates for farmland and manufactured homes, shown under the calendar below.

The October 15, 2026 installment has already passed. If it is still open on your parcel, the penalty schedule in Minnesota Statutes 279.01 applies. Late fees start at 2 percent for a homestead and 4 percent for everything else, double once the next month begins, and then creep up 1 percent per month until they hit a ceiling of 8 percent (homestead) or 12 percent (other property).

Two details help when a payment is close to the line. Very small bills, $100 or under, come due in one lump on May 15. And the statute gives a one-time break: a mailed check whose postmark is no more than one business day late can have its penalty erased, once per owner. If you mail near a deadline, ask a postal clerk for a hand-applied postmark.

Olmsted County property tax calendar for Rochester owners (source: Olmsted County Property Records and Licensing)
DateWhat happens
February 1Exempt property applications due
Mid-MarchValuation notices and tax statements mailed
Mid-AprilLocal board of appeal meetings begin
April 30Tax Court petition deadline
May 15First half of real estate tax due
Mid-JuneCounty board of appeal and equalization meets
October 15Second half of real property tax due
December 15Homestead applications due

Farm second halves and manufactured home second halves fall on November 16, 2026. The manufactured home first half was due August 31, 2026.

How do I pay my Olmsted County tax bill from Rochester?

The county takes payment several ways. Whichever you pick, quote the parcel ID from your statement; a real property ID looks like RP 74.05.05.000000.

  • Online, through the county's property information site: card at 3.28 percent or e-check at $3.16, current year only, capped at $300,000. Allow seven to 10 business days for the bank to clear it and wait for the confirmation email.
  • Phone: 1-800-272-9829, jurisdiction number 3336. This line also accepts back-year tax at the same rates.
  • Mail: check or money order made out to Olmsted County, plus the stub, with five to seven business days of postal transit.
  • Counter: cash, check, money order or card at the Government Center, where cards add 2.15 percent. Drop boxes are there too.
  • Your bank's bill pay: the parcel ID serves as the account number, and the county counts the day it receives the money.

A free ACH withdrawal program also exists. In 2026 its sign-up cutoffs were April 10 for May and September 11 for October, with money pulled on May 10 and October 10. Selling can end an enrollment, judged by the date the deed is recorded, so notify the office in writing if a sale lands near a withdrawal.

What is Rochester like for someone selling a house there?

Rochester sits on the South Fork of the Zumbro River in southeast Minnesota, about 85 miles from Minneapolis and Saint Paul, and its housing market follows the medical economy built around Mayo Clinic. Settlement began in 1854 at Head's Tavern, a log cabin put up by George and Henrietta Head, and incorporation came in 1858. When the 1883 tornado struck, William Mayo and his sons treated the injured, and St. Marys Hospital opened in 1889.

Mayo Clinic is the core employer, and the 2013 Destination Medical Center law set up a state-backed plan for downtown districts around the clinic and the river. IBM's campus and Rochester Public Schools are also among the larger employers listed for the city. After a major flood in 1978 the city reworked rivers and streams in a costly flood-control program, a useful fact if a buyer asks about low-lying lots.

Weather leaves marks on Rochester houses. Yearly snowfall averages 51.9 inches, rainfall about 33 inches, and the city ranks among the windiest in the country. Tornadoes struck the Lincolnshire area on the northwest side in June 2010 and parts of southwest Rochester in June 2019. The Census Bureau gives these figures for the city:

  • Typical owner-occupied home value, 2020 to 2024: $310,500, with $332,700 as the national figure.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 65.1 percent, across 51,131 households of about 2.34 people.
  • Median gross rent: $1,399. Median owner cost with a mortgage: $1,864 a month.
  • Share of residents in the same home a year before: 83.0 percent, below the national 87.7 percent.

How do I challenge a Rochester property valuation?

Begin with the assessor's office at 507-328-7670, carrying a recent appraisal or sale prices of comparable homes.

Still unsettled? Attend a meeting from the schedule on your valuation notice. Places with their own local board start there, and the rest go directly to the county board. By statute, local boards sit between April 1 and May 31 and can lower the assessor's overall total by no more than 1 percent. The county board follows in mid-June.

Final recourse is the Minnesota Tax Court, with a petition due by April 30 of the year the tax is payable. A 2023 change also requires a copy to reach the county auditor. Olmsted County takes that copy by email at olmcotaxpetitionservice@olmstedcounty.gov or by hand at the County Attorney's Office. The Tax Court's phone number is 651-539-3260.

Which relief programs can lower a Rochester owner's tax?

State programs do most of the work, and the county lists them for Rochester owners. Homestead applications are due December 15 and exempt property applications February 1. Green Acres applications for farmland are due May 1.

  • Regular property tax refund, often called the circuit breaker, based on household income and the tax you pay.
  • Special refund, available when net tax rises by at least 12 percent and $100, with no income test. Both refunds use Form M1PR.
  • Senior citizen property tax deferral, applied for through the Minnesota Department of Revenue on Form CR-SCD.
  • Credit of $120 per month served for members of the military in a combat zone or hazardous duty area.

Notices of proposed taxes, the Truth in Taxation mailing, go out in mid-November. They project next year's bill if each taxing body adopts the budget now on the table, and they list hearing dates.

What happens to unpaid tax when I sell a Rochester house?

A past-due balance stays with the parcel, so ask the county for the exact payoff at 507-328-7635 before closing. Taxes left unpaid long enough can lead to forfeiture, with title passing to the State of Minnesota.

A sale also changes who gets the mail. The county sends one statement a year in late March, to the address you gave at closing, and sends none for mid-year purchases. Tax information may also show up in your closing papers. Once a deed is recorded, the assessor removes homestead status from the next assessment year unless the new owner applies and qualifies (Minnesota Statutes 272.115).

If your Rochester house has tax behind and you want a quick sale, pull together the parcel ID, your latest statement and the payoff figure first. If automatic withdrawal is on, send the county a written stop request, since a recorded transfer may end it only after the recording date.

More questions about Rochester, MN Property Tax Guide

Who collects property tax in Rochester, MN?

The county's Property Records and Licensing office takes the payments, and the county assessor sets values. For statement questions call 507-328-7636.

Is the second half of 2026 Rochester property tax still payable?

It can be paid, but it is late. The date was October 15, 2026, and penalties grow each month. Farm and manufactured home second halves are due November 16, 2026.

Can I pay Rochester property tax by credit card?

Yes. Card payments online or by phone add 3.28 percent, and an e-check adds $3.16. At the Government Center counter the card surcharge is 2.15 percent.

How do I get a copy of my Rochester tax statement?

Print one from the county's property information website or call 507-328-7636. Reprints at the office cost $2.

Does automatic withdrawal stop when I sell my Rochester home?

Not always right away. The county says a transfer of the property may end the enrollment, but the timing follows the recording date of the deed and is not guaranteed. Tell the county in writing if a withdrawal date is near.
